- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or apply decay factor of 0.75 to subsequent values.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x true outcome, apply downward adjustment proportional to sentiment decay (e.g., 0.5x sentiment weight).
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment flips from high to low within 5 days, reduce forecast by 20–40% in next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates downward moves in low-sentiment periods; if sentiment drops below 0.33 for 3+ consecutive days, add 10–20% buffer to forecast to account for risk aversion.
